paper_title: Random Reed-Solomon Codes and Random Linear Codes are Locally Equivalent
authors: Matan Levi (Ben-Gurion University, Israel), Jonathan Mosheiff (Ben-Gurion University, Israel), Nikhil Shagrithaya (University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, USA)

statement: [MRRSW20] is designed for smaller alphabets. Our goal is to unify these approaches into a single framework that works uniformly across all alphabet sizes. Currently, RLCs are shown to achieve the Elias bound for list-decodability in two cases: when q is constant L or when q ≥ 2Ω( ε ) , leaving a gap between these two regimes. This gap highlights the differences between the two methods used to study local properties. The proof for the constant q case [GHK11] aligns well with the classical local properties framework, whereas our proof for the large q case (Corollary III.6) is captured within the LCL framework. Developing a unified local property framework may provide a uniform proof that RLCs achieve the Elias bound across all alphabet sizes. 3) Optimality of Random Linear Codes: In the large q regime, RLCs and random RS codes are essentially optimally list-decodable, as they approach the generalized Singleton bound. We conjecture that this optimality extends more broadly within the class of linear codes and holds for all LCL properties (see Section II-C for a formal definition).
context: Another challenge arises in the small q regime, such as when q = poly(ℓ). Our current methods cannot directly address list-recoverability in this setting due to the exponential dependence of q on locality. Relaxing this dependence is an important goal, as it could deepen our understanding of list-recovery in this regime. Furthermore, extending our framework to analyze highly non-local properties would be valuable. Consider the following example: fix a large q and let 0 < R < 1, q (1−R) < ℓ < q, and ε > 0. Let P represent the property of (0, ℓ, L)-list-recoverability for codes in Fnq , where L = ℓn · q −(1−R)n · (1 + ε). Note that P is not a local property, since L is typically exponential in n, but it is a natural one to consider. Notice that ℓn ·q −(1−R)n is the expected size of the set C ∩ Z1 × Z2 × · · · × Zn , where C ⊆ Fnq is a fixed code of rate (1 − R), and Z1 , . . . , Zn are independent uniformly random subsets of Fq of size ℓ. Thus, a code C satisfies P if its maximum intersection with any product set Z1 × Z2 × · · · × Zn is at most (1 + ε) times this expectation. From a pseudorandomness perspective, a code satisfying P can be said to fool product sets (also known as combinatorial rectangles) within a (1 + ε) factor. Consider the question of whether any linear code satisfies this property. In particular, do RLCs satisfy it? Both questions were essentially answered in the affirmative by [MPSW21] when R > 12 and q is a large prime. For R ≤ 12 , these questions remain open. We conjecture that the answer is again positive, provided that q is a sufficiently large prime. 2) An Alphabet-Uniform Framework: As discussed in Remark III.3, the LCL framework developed here is well-suited for sufficiently large alphabets. For instance, Corollary III.6 on the list-decodability of RLCs applies L when q ≥ 2Ω( ε ) , where ε is the gap to capacity. In contrast, the classical local property framework from [MRRSW20] is designed for smaller alphabets. Our goal is to unify these approaches into a single framework that works uniformly across all alphabet sizes. Currently, RLCs are shown to achieve the Elias bound for list-decodability in two cases: when q is constant L or when q ≥ 2Ω( ε ) , leaving a gap between these two regimes. This gap highlights the differences between the two methods used to study local properties. The proof for the constant q case [GHK11] aligns well with the classical local properties framework, whereas our proof for the large q case (Corollary III.6) is captured within the LCL framework. Developing a unified local property framework may provide a uniform proof that RLCs achieve the Elias bound across all alphabet sizes. 3) Optimality of Random Linear Codes: In the large q regime, RLCs and random RS codes are essentially optimally list-decodable, as they approach the generalized Singleton bound. We conjecture that this optimality extends more broadly within the class of linear codes and holds for all LCL properties (see Section II-C for a formal definition). Conjecture I.1 (Optimality of RLCs and random RS codes for LCL properties). For every ε > 0 and b ∈ N, there exist constants n0 and q0 such that the following holds: Let P be a b-local (monotone-decreasing) LCL property. If q ≥ q0 and n ≥ n0 , then any linear code in Fnq with rate at least RP + ε does not satisfy P. Following the original publication of this paper, [LS25] essentially proved the conjecture for the case of list-recoverability, by proving nearly tight upper bounds on the output list size (which is equivalent to proving an upper bound on the threshol rate corresponding to a fixed output list size). If the conjecture is true, then it would simultaneously generalize this negative result for list-recovery and the generalized Singleton bound. II. P RELIMINARIES A.
